subject: Partial write timeouts on hosted inference (investigating)
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@cognitiveai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Partial write timeouts on hosted inference (investigating)

Hi Maya,

I wanted to reach out proactively — we are currently investigating a transient increase in write-timeout errors affecting a subset of hosted inference requests (you may see intermittent 504/500s for short windows). Early telemetry shows the errors started around 08:05 PDT and peaked between 08:20–08:40.

What we know so far:
- Impact: ~2–4% of requests to generation endpoints in us-west experienced write-timeouts to our KV/cache layer, manifesting as 504s or short stalls.
- Scope: a portion of traffic for models using prefix-caching; not all customers were affected.
- Mitigation in progress: we rolled a conservative retry/backoff at the ingress layer and expanded routing to fallback edges. That has reduced customer-facing failures while we investigate root cause.

We have published an incident on our status page (INC-20280522-PTW) and will post updates as we have them: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-20280522-PTW

If you can share whether you saw client-side retries spike or any downstream errors on your side (timeouts, partial responses), that would be helpful. We're treating this as priority and I'll follow up with a technical summary shortly.

Apologies for the disruption — I'm looping in our on-call infra lead (Aditya) and your account lead (Lauren) so we can coordinate communication.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: diagnostic_logs_20280522.zip (attached to later update)
From: Maya Patel <maya@cognitiveai.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
Cc: CognitiveAI SRE <sre@cognitiveai.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 08:20:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial write timeouts on hosted inference (investigating)

Thanks for the heads up, Rohan.

We did see a small bump in error rates on our side around 08:25 — primarily synchronous invocations that returned 504s. A few user requests surfaced truncated responses. We applied a short client-side retry and that helped, but would like to understand if tokens could have been dropped or if we should expect duplicate completions.

Also: is there any recommended mitigation on our end while you continue to investigate? Should we route to another region or alter our retry/backoff?

— Maya
Maya Patel
Head of ML Product
CognitiveAI

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 08:45:12 -0700
Subject: Internal: quick on-call note and mitigation summary

Rohan / Aditya — quick run of the on-call findings to keep the customer loop concise: 

Timeline summary (internal):
- 08:05 PDT: telemetry shows rising write latencies to prefix-cache coordinator in us-west.
- 08:18 PDT: first customer-facing 504s reported; error budget alert fired.
- 08:22 PDT: ingress retries/backoff enabled (conservative settings).
- 08:30 PDT: additional routing to standby edge pool; error rate drops but residual 0.5–1.5% failures persist.
- 08:40 PDT: team rolled a configuration change that increased connection pool and relaxed a tight circuit-breaker threshold — immediate drop to baseline by 08:48.

Root-cause hypothesis (initial): a short-lived spike in cache write amplification combined with a circuit-breaker being too aggressive under a particular sequence-length distribution. We are pulling detailed kernel and cache coordinator traces.

Next actions (assigned):
- Aditya: collect and sanitize KV coordinator logs and provide artifact (diagnostic_logs_20280522.zip) — ETA 11:00 PDT.
- Rohan: update customer (done) and post statuspage update with incident ID (done).
- Lauren: coordinate with customer success for any credit/SLAs if impact proves material.
- Engineering: formal postmortem to be shared within 72 hours; interim RCA by EOD.

Keep Rohan & Maya in the loop for customer-facing messages. We should avoid overpromising while we confirm root cause.

— Lauren
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@cognitiveai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident update: write-timeouts mitigated; next steps and artifacts

Hi Maya — quick update and next steps now that we've stabilized service.

Update:
- Mitigation applied: ingress retries + routing to standby edges + conservative circuit-breaker tuning. Errors returned to baseline (~<0.2%) by ~08:48 PDT.
- Impact summary: transient partial failures for ~2–4% of requests for customers leveraging prefix-caching configurations in us-west between 08:05–08:48 PDT.
- Duplicate/dropped tokens: our initial analysis indicates no token loss at the model output layer; some requests returned 504s before the generation completed, so clients that retried may receive duplicate completions. We suggest client-side idempotency keys where dedup is required.

Artifacts and next steps:
- Attached: diagnostic_logs_20280522.zip (sanitized traces from KV coordinator and ingress)
- Status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-20280522-PTW (incident summary and timeline updated)
- Detailed postmortem: engineering will publish an RCA and follow-up actions within 72 hours; we'll include concrete mitigations (kernel patch and circuit-breaker tuning, improved autoscaling rules).

Recommended short-term action for CognitiveAI:
- If you observed retries, consider idempotency or client-side dedup during the 08:05–08:48 window.
- If you prefer, we can route your traffic to eu-central as temporary mitigation — reach out and we can coordinate a brief maintenance window.

Again, very sorry for the disruption. We'll share the full postmortem and the timeline once it's complete. Please let me know if you want a quick call to walk through the logs.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: diagnostic_logs_20280522.zip (2.2MB)
